page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.32xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz, delivering 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. The processor architecture includes 54 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction sets such as AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic accelerators like AES and SHA-NI. The server is configured with 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio.

Storage and networking subsystems are heavily provisioned. The instance includes 7,600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage for high-speed temporary or caching requirements, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps. It does not include discrete GPUs, relying solely on CPU compute capability.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing and I/O scalability. The instance scores in the top tier for PassMark CPU metrics, including encryption (110,839.05) and extended instruction execution (106,439.63), while multi-core stress-ng (123,845.94) and Geekbench multi-core (16,603.0) place it firmly in the top 25%. Read-only memory bandwidth reaches 334.82 GB/sec on large blocks. Conversely, single-thread metrics such as Geekbench single-core (1697.0) and stress-ng single-core (1891.9) reflect average performance consistent with general-purpose multi-socket deployments.

This hardware profile offers solid cost efficiency for large multi-threaded environments that require co-located high-speed local NVMe storage and vast network throughput without paying for GPU overhead. Primary workload fits include large enterprise relational databases, distributed in-memory data grids, Redis deployments, static web delivery platforms, software compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services m6idn.32xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose instance powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors operating at 3.5 GHz. Configured on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores, 512 GB of DDR4 RAM, 7,600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage, and 200 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The system contains no discrete GPUs. Multi-core performance is robust, showing top-tier PassMark CPU and encryption results, backed by strong multi-threaded compression, Redis throughput reaching 109.07 million operations per second, and rapid memory bandwidth. While single-threaded compute performance is average, the massive core density, combined NVMe storage, and 200 Gbps networking make this configuration suitable for high-concurrency databases, large-scale Redis caches, static content serving, software build systems, and distributed enterprise backend workloads.
